Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $36\div 9=4$, $4$ is known as the
questions.corrige_markdown: In a division $36\div 9=4$ the number divided (36) is the dividend, the number we divide by (9) is the divisor, and the result (4) is the quotient. There is no remainder because 9 goes into 36 exactly. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The next prime number greater than $23$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. Test the numbers after 23: $24$ is even; $25=5\times 5$; $26$ is even; $27=3\times 9$; $28$ is even; $29$ has no divisor other than 1 and 29, so it is prime. The trap is to jump to 31, which is prime but is not the next one. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The absolute value of $-1-9$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: First evaluate the expression inside: $-1-9=-10$. The absolute value gives the distance from zero, so it is never negative: $|-10|=10$. Option A forgets to take the absolute value. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Converting $0.15$ to a fraction in its simplest form gives
questions.corrige_markdown: $0.15=\frac{15}{100}$. Divide the numerator and the denominator by their H.C.F. which is 5: $\frac{15\div 5}{100\div 5}=\frac{3}{20}$. Option B is correct in value but not simplified, and C comes from a wrong place value. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Expressing $0.0597$ in standard form gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Standard form is $a\times 10^{n}$ with $1\le a<10$. Move the decimal point two places to the right to get $5.97$, so the power of ten is $-2$ (the number is smaller than 1): $0.0597=5.97\times 10^{-2}$. Options C and D round the number to 2 significant figures, which the question does not ask. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number of significant figures in $14.501$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Every non-zero digit is significant, and a zero placed between non-zero digits is also significant. The digits 1, 4, 5, 0, 1 are all significant, so there are 5 significant figures. The trap is to ignore the zero and answer 4. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mary went to bed at $11:20$ pm and asked John to wake her up after $2$ hours. The time by the clock that John woke up Mary is
questions.corrige_markdown: $11:20$ pm plus 2 hours gives $1:20$ in the morning of the next day (11:20 pm + 40 min = midnight, then 1 h 20 min more). The clock shows $1:20$. Options B and D are 1:20 in the afternoon (13:20 on the 24-hour clock), and A mixes the two notations. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An article is sold at a loss of $10\%$. Given that the selling price is $7{,}200$ FCFA, the cost price in FCFA is
questions.corrige_markdown: A loss of $10\%$ means the selling price is $90\%$ of the cost price. So $0.9\times \text{cost}=7200$ and $\text{cost}=\frac{7200}{0.9}=8000$ FCFA. Check: $10\%$ of $8000$ is $800$ and $8000-800=7200$. The trap is to add $10\%$ to $7200$ (option A) or to subtract it (option B). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that six textbooks each of the same price cost $30{,}000$ FCFA. The cost in FCFA of three textbooks is
questions.corrige_markdown: Three textbooks are half of six textbooks, so they cost half of the price: $\frac{30000}{2}=15000$ FCFA. (One textbook costs $30000\div 6=5000$ FCFA, and $3\times 5000=15000$.) Option A is the price of only one textbook. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The scale of a map is $1:50{,}000$. The actual length in km of a road measuring $4$ cm on the map is
questions.corrige_markdown: Actual length $=4\times 50000=200000$ cm. Convert: $200000$ cm $=2000$ m $=2$ km. The common slip is a wrong conversion between cm, m and km (option B or D). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the sets $A$ and $B$, such that $A=\{1,2,3,4\}$ and $B=\{2,4,6,8\}$. The sets $A$ and $B$ are called
questions.corrige_markdown: Two sets are equivalent when they have the same number of elements: $n(A)=4$ and $n(B)=4$. They are not equal, because equal sets contain exactly the same elements (here $1$ and $3$ are not in $B$). $A$ is not a subset of $B$ since $1\notin B$, and a power set is the set of all subsets of a set, which is not the case here. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $P$ and $Q$ are disjoint sets. The relationship between $P$ and $Q$ in set notation is

*Options as printed:* A) $P\cup Q=\phi$   B) $n(P\cap Q)=0$   C) $P\cap Q=(\phi)$   D) $P=Q$
questions.corrige_markdown:
Disjoint sets have no element in common, so their intersection is the empty set: $P\cap Q=\phi$, which means $n(P\cap Q)=0$. Option A would mean that both sets are empty, and D would mean that the sets are equal. Options B and C both express this relation (C is $P\cap Q=\phi$ with extra brackets), so the printed question has two valid answers.

**Intended answer: $P\cap Q=\phi$, that is $n(P\cap Q)=0$ (options B and C).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The shaded region in figure 1 is represented as

![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In figure 1 the dotted (shaded) part is everything inside the rectangle $\varepsilon$ that lies outside both circles $A$ and $B$. The part inside the two circles together is $A\cup B$, so the region outside both is its complement: $(A\cup B)'$. Option A is the unshaded part. Options B and D are the same set, $(A\cap B)'=A'\cup B'$, which would shade everything except the overlap. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The negation of "Some students will pass the examination" is
questions.corrige_markdown: "Some students will pass" means at least one student passes. Its negation must say that this is false: not even one student passes, that is "No student will pass the examination". Option D is not the negation: it says more than the opposite of the statement, and B means that every student passes. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: No student will pass the examination
No student will not pass the examination
All students will not pass the examination
All students will pass the examination

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 2 is an arrow diagram of a relation between $P$ and $Q$. The range of the relation is

![fig-2](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In the figure the arrows go $a\to 1$, $b\to 3$ and $c\to 4$. The range is the set of elements of $Q$ that are actually reached by an arrow: $\{1,3,4\}$. $\{a,b,c\}$ is the domain, $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ is the whole set $Q$ (the codomain), and $\{2,5\}$ is the set of elements of $Q$ that are NOT reached. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the function, $f(x)=1-2x$. The value of $f(-3)$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Substitute $x=-3$: $f(-3)=1-2(-3)=1+6=7$. The trap is the sign: $-2\times(-3)=+6$, not $-6$ (which would give $-5$). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: $A$ and $B$ are two sets such that $A=\{3,4\}$ and $B=\{x,y\}$, the cartesian product $A\times B$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The cartesian product $A\times B$ is the SET of all ordered pairs $(a,b)$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$. With 2 elements in each set there are $2\times 2=4$ pairs: $(3,x),(3,y),(4,x),(4,y)$, written between braces. Option A has only two pairs, B is not a set of pairs, and D lists the right pairs but without the braces of a set. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The function $f$ is defined on $\mathbb{R}$, the set of real numbers by $f:x\mapsto 3x-2$, $f^{-1}:x\mapsto$
questions.corrige_markdown: Put $y=3x-2$ and make $x$ the subject: $y+2=3x$, so $x=\frac{y+2}{3}$. Swapping the letters, $f^{-1}:x\mapsto\frac{x+2}{3}$. Check: $f(4)=10$ and $f^{-1}(10)=\frac{12}{3}=4$. Option B subtracts 2 instead of adding it back. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A polygon having nine sides is called
questions.corrige_markdown: The names are: heptagon 7 sides, octagon 8, nonagon 9, decagon 10. A polygon with nine sides is a nonagon. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The sum of the three interior angles of a triangle is
questions.corrige_markdown: The interior angles of any triangle add up to $180^\circ$. ($360^\circ$ is the sum for a quadrilateral.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number of lines of symmetry in a rhombus is/are
questions.corrige_markdown: A rhombus that is not a square has two lines of symmetry, which are its two diagonals. It has no line of symmetry through the midpoints of the opposite sides (those belong to a rectangle or a square). Four lines belong to a square. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 3 is a circle with center $O$ and a chord $PQ$ subtending an angle of $70^\circ$ at the centre, $O$. The value of the angle marked $\theta$ is

![fig-3](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The label $\theta$ is not legible on the printed figure; the angle asked is the angle at the circumference standing on the chord $PQ$, that is angle $PRQ$ at $R$. By the circle theorem, the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc: $\theta=\frac{70^\circ}{2}=35^\circ$. The value $55^\circ=\frac{180^\circ-70^\circ}{2}$ would be the base angle of the isosceles triangle $OPQ$, and $70^\circ$ is the angle at the centre itself. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 4 represents the net of

![fig-4](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: Figure 4 is a plain rectangle with no circles. Rolling a rectangle into a tube gives the curved surface of a cylinder, with no circular top or bottom. So it is the net of an open cylinder. A closed cylinder would need two circles (the top and the bottom) in its net. A rectangle is a shape, not a solid, so option A is not a net, and C is wrong because the figure is not a square. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 5 is a rectangular based Pyramid. The number of edges is:

![fig-5](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The rectangular base has 4 edges. Four more edges join the apex (top point) to the four corners of the base. Total: $4+4=8$ edges. The number 5 is the number of faces (vertices too), not edges. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 6 is a circle with centre $O$. The shaded region in the figure is called a

![fig-6](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The shaded region is bounded by two radii (the lines from the centre $O$) and the arc between them. A region of this kind is a sector. A segment is bounded by a chord and an arc, a chord is a line, and a secant is a line that cuts the circle at two points. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The perimeter of a rectangle with length $x$ units and width $y$ units in terms of $x$ and $y$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths, so the perimeter is $x+y+x+y=2(x+y)$. The product $xy$ is the area. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 7 is a right-angled triangle with sides $6$ cm, $x$ cm and area $24$ cm$^2$. The value of $x$ in the figure is

![fig-7](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base $x$ and the height $6$. Area $=\frac{1}{2}\times\text{base}\times\text{height}$, so $\frac{1}{2}\times x\times 6=24$, that is $3x=24$ and $x=8$. The trap is to forget the factor $\frac{1}{2}$ (then $6x=24$ gives $x=4$). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The volume in cm$^3$ of a cone with height $10$ cm and base radius $6$ cm in terms of $\pi$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\frac{1}{3}\times\pi\times 6^2\times 10=\frac{360\pi}{3}=120\pi$ cm$^3$. Option B forgets the factor $\frac{1}{3}$ (that would be the volume of a cylinder). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The $y$-intercept of the line $y=2x+4$ on the cartesian plane is
questions.corrige_markdown: The line crosses the $y$-axis where $x=0$: $y=2(0)+4=4$. In $y=mx+c$ the intercept is $c=4$; the number 2 is the gradient. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The gradient of the line $3y=6x-3$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Divide every term by 3 to write the line as $y=mx+c$: $y=2x-1$. The gradient is the coefficient of $x$, so $m=2$. The trap is to read 6 directly from $3y=6x-3$ before dividing by 3. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The equation of the line $l$ in the cartesian plane shown in figure 8 is

![fig-8](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In figure 8 the line $l$ is horizontal and crosses the $y$-axis at the mark $4$. Every point on it has $y=4$, whatever the value of $x$, so its equation is $y=4$. A vertical line would be $x=4$, and $y=4x$ or $4y=x$ are lines through the origin. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Subtracting $2+b$ from $2a+b$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Subtracting $2+b$ from $2a+b$ means $(2a+b)-(2+b)=2a+b-2-b=2a-2$. The trap is to write $(2+b)-(2a+b)$ (the wrong order, option A) or to forget that the minus sign applies to $b$ as well (option D). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The value of the expression $x^2-y$ when $x=3$ and $y=2$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $x^2-y=3^2-2=9-2=7$. Option D comes from $3\times 2-2$ (treating $x^2$ as $2x$), and C from adding instead of subtracting. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The range of values of $x$ for which $7-2x\le 19$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $7-2x\le 19$ gives $-2x\le 12$. Dividing both sides by $-2$ reverses the inequality sign: $x\ge -6$. Check with $x=0$: $7\le 19$ is true, and $0\ge -6$. The trap is to keep the sign unchanged (option B). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Factorizing $x^2+4x+3$ completely gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Look for two numbers with product $3$ and sum $4$: they are $1$ and $3$. So $x^2+4x+3=(x+1)(x+3)$. Check by expanding: $x^2+3x+x+3=x^2+4x+3$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Simplifying $2^{-3}$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: A negative index means a reciprocal: $2^{-3}=\frac{1}{2^3}=\frac{1}{8}$. The result is positive; options C and D come from multiplying $2\times 3$ instead of $2^3$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The next term of the sequence $-3, 1, 5, \ldots$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The difference between consecutive terms is $1-(-3)=4$ and $5-1=4$. It is an arithmetic sequence with common difference 4, so the next term is $5+4=9$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The number of even nodes in the network in figure 9 is

![fig-9](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_9.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: A node is even when an even number of arcs meet there (its degree is even). Reading figure 9: the two nodes on the left each have degree 2, the central node has degree 4, and each of the two nodes on the right has degree 3 (the straight arc, the curved arc and one arc to the centre). So the even nodes are the two left nodes and the centre node: 3 even nodes. The two right-hand nodes are odd. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The relationship that exists between $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$ and $\tan\theta$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: From SOH CAH TOA, $\sin\theta=\frac{O}{H}$, $\cos\theta=\frac{A}{H}$ and $\tan\theta=\frac{O}{A}$. Dividing, $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{O/H}{A/H}=\frac{O}{A}=\tan\theta$. Option A is the inverse ratio (cotangent). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 10 is a right-angled triangle with sides $n$, $8$ cm and $6$ cm. The value of $n$ is

![fig-10](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_10.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In figure 10, $n$ is the side opposite the right angle (the hypotenuse). By Pythagoras' theorem, $n^2=6^2+8^2=36+64=100$, so $n=10$ cm. Option A adds the two sides ($6+8=14$). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 11 shows a bearing of $S$ from $R$. The bearing of $R$ from $S$ is

![fig-11](gce-ol-maths-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_11.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The bearing of $S$ from $R$ is $026^\circ$. The bearing of $R$ from $S$ is the back bearing: add $180^\circ$ when the bearing is less than $180^\circ$. $026^\circ+180^\circ=206^\circ$. The values $154^\circ$ ($180^\circ-26^\circ$) and $116^\circ$ ($90^\circ+26^\circ$) are common wrong answers. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the vectors $\vec r=\begin{pmatrix}-3\\6\end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec p=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$, evaluating $\vec r+\vec p$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Add the components one by one: $\begin{pmatrix}-3+1\\6+(-1)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\5\end{pmatrix}$. Options A and B come from a sign mistake on the first component. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the vector $\overrightarrow{OP}=-4\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$, $|\overrightarrow{OP}|=$
questions.corrige_markdown: The magnitude is $|\overrightarrow{OP}|=\sqrt{(-4)^2+3^2}=\sqrt{16+9}=\sqrt{25}=5$. Option B adds the components ($4+3$) and D forgets the square root. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The direction of the vector $-3\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The vector $\begin{pmatrix}-3\\-3\end{pmatrix}$ points to the left and downwards, in the third quadrant. Its reference angle is $\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{3}=45^\circ$. Measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis, the direction is $180^\circ+45^\circ=225^\circ$ (this is also the compass bearing of due south-west, so the answer is the same with both conventions). The value $45^\circ$ is the direction of $3\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$, the opposite vector. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The order of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-1&0&3\end{pmatrix}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The order of a matrix is (number of rows) $\times$ (number of columns). This matrix has 1 row and 3 columns, so its order is $1\times 3$. Option A reverses the two numbers. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The transpose of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-3&1&5\\0&2&7\end{pmatrix}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The transpose is obtained by writing the rows as columns. Row 1 $(-3,\ 1,\ 5)$ becomes column 1 and row 2 $(0,\ 2,\ 7)$ becomes column 2, giving a $3\times 2$ matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-3&0\\1&2\\5&7\end{pmatrix}$. Option B swaps the columns, C reverses the order of the rows and columns (a rotation), and D mixes the entries. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The range of the distribution $2, 4, 2, 6, 3, 7, -1$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Range $=$ largest value $-$ smallest value $=7-(-1)=8$. The trap is to forget that the smallest value is negative and compute $7-1=6$ or take $7$. The number 23 is the sum of the data. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The median of the distribution $7, 3, 1, 1, 4, 7, 0$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Arrange the 7 values in order: $0,\ 1,\ 1,\ 3,\ 4,\ 7,\ 7$. The median is the middle (4th) value, which is $3$. The mistake is to take the middle of the unordered list (which gives 1). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the distribution $8, 9, 6, 8, 15, 8, 11, 7$. The mode is
questions.corrige_markdown: The mode is the value that occurs most often. The value 8 appears three times and every other value appears once, so the mode is $8$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The probability that Susan goes to the farm is $\frac{2}{5}$. The probability that she does not go to the farm is
questions.corrige_markdown: The probabilities of an event and of its complement add up to 1. So $P(\text{not go})=1-\frac{2}{5}=\frac{3}{5}$. Option C is the probability of the event itself. **Answer: A.**
